recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-23924; related package-quantity clarifications such as FHIR-39130 can be audited separately if assigned as their own reconciliation seeds.
issue_request: FHIR-23924 was a Published FHIR-core BR&R change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking how to model several package configurations of the same manufactured item. The resolution was to move the count to the referring item in PackagedProductDefinition instead of having ManufacturedItemDefinition count itself.
initial_application: No explicit FHIR-23924-tagged source commit was found. Source history immediately after the originating September 2019 Zulip discussion moved count semantics to the packaged level in 6f506840ae, removed ManufacturedItemDefinition.quantity and added a contained item amount in 7512379e82, and added explanatory ManufacturedItemDefinition narrative in b0893a67ea.
additional_context: The current R5/R6-era resource names are ManufacturedItemDefinition and PackagedProductDefinition; source/fhir.ini keeps them active and redirects old MedicinalProductManufactured/MedicinalProductPackaged names to them. Later Published issue FHIR-39130 confirmed the same modeling rule by clarifying that PackagedProductDefinition.packaging.containedItem.amount carries item amount or continuous quantity, not ManufacturedItemDefinition.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source has no ManufacturedItemDefinition.quantity element, defines PackagedProductDefinition.packaging.containedItem.amount for the number or quantity of the contained item, and includes narrative/examples explaining that one manufactured item can be reused across package definitions with different quantities.

related_jiras.note: Later Published clarification says containedItem.amount, not ManufacturedItemDefinition, carries continuous manufactured item quantities.
